name: 48442-promptembeds-gemma3-12b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1), driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1 -- one vLLM engine on one GPU with `distributed-executor-backend: mp`, which is not the one-GPU default and puts the model worker in a process of its own.
architecture: Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration, text tower used alone: 48 layers, hidden 3840, 16 query / 8 KV heads, head_dim 256, vocabulary 262208, bf16, ~12.2B params (~24.4 GB), window 131072.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=8, bounded at 240 requests with a 900 s safety cap, 10% warmup and 10% cooldown, static seed 48442.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn, 8192 prompt tokens and 4 output tokens, both with min == max. Every request is sent as precomputed input embeddings rather than token ids (`scenario.json: spec.backend.prompt_embeds`, and `enable-prompt-embeds: true` in vllm-config.yaml), so each carries 8192 x 3840 bf16 = 60.0 MiB. GuideLLM draws a fresh synthetic body per request: the length is pinned, the content is not.
purpose: A 12-billion Gemma-class document assistant taking eight-thousand-token precomputed prompt embeddings with terse replies, eight concurrent users, one GPU.
launch:
model: unsloth/gemma-3-12b-it

tensor-parallel-size: 1
pipeline-parallel-size: 1
distributed-executor-backend: mp

dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 8260
enable-prefix-caching: false
enforce-eager: true

# requests arrive as precomputed input embeddings; the engine refuses them without this.
enable-prompt-embeds: true

# pinned, not defaulted: an in-process engine build falls through to 128 / 2048.
max-num-seqs: 16
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# NOT 0.90, and the reason is arithmetic rather than tuning. At most 16 sequences are resident
# (`max-num-seqs`) and KV at 8260 positions is 8 global layers x 8260 x 8192 B + 40 sliding(1024)
# layers x 1024 x 8192 B = 877 MB per sequence, so the workload's ceiling is ~14 GB of KV. 0.55
# reserves 43.5 GiB per card, of which ~22.7 GiB is weights and ~3 GiB is the eager 8192-token
# activation peak, leaving ~17.8 GiB -- still above the 14 GB ceiling, so no request is ever
# preempted or queued for blocks, exactly as under 0.90's ~47 GB. Prefix caching is off, so pool
# size has no other effect. What it buys: at 0.90 the engine demands 71.3 GiB FREE at startup and
# refuses to construct if anything at all is left on the card.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.55
